blocks.text: General requirements
Sign into site and ensure arrangements are made with the Principal Contractor for work to commence.
All operatives will receive a site-specific induction from the Principal Contractor before work commences.
Assess working area for access and egress and potential hazards. Report any hazards identified to the Principal Contractor.
Temporary works designs will be provided by the Principal Contractor. Operatives must work in line with these requirements.
Good working methods will be employed in line with the RAMS.
Chamber Joist Installation
Ensure the scaffold and internal fall protection is safe to work on with the Principal Contractor.
Any defects identified by the operatives must be reported to the Principal Contractor immediately and work must be stopped until the Principal Contractor has addressed the issues.

Arrangements will be made for the materials to be loaded into the working areas. This will include chamber joists and floorboards. A Tele Handler will be required to load chamber joists and floorboards. Ensure these materials are loaded into the loading bay area and then distributed into the work area. Do not overload any areas and do not load full packs of floorboards onto chamber joist.

In situations where there are significant variations in floor levels on adjoining plots and there is a risk of falls between plots of more than 900mm joiners will fit the chamber joists on highest plot first from the existing working platforms. Fall protection will be fitted first before the floorboards are fitted to ensure there are no falls into the adjoining plots.
Commence fitting chamber joists and floorboards in line with the manufacturer’s guidance and sequence of works.

Temporary stairwell handrail protection must be fitted as soon as the staircases have been installed. No work on the floor above must be undertaken until they are fitted to the correct standards and fully surround the stairwell opening. The principal Contractor will provide the posts and materials for this, and the installation instructions will be given to operatives.

When cutting out staircase openings a system of work will be adopted to ensure there is no fall from height risks. The opening will be cut from above and the floor will be removed from below to eliminate any internal falls into the plot.
All glues and adhesives will be used in line with the specific COSHH assessments.
First Fix Installation
Set up work area and place warning signs where required.

The working at height control measures will be fitted in priority to all other working activities. Stairwell fall protection will be fitted first to ensure joiners are not exposed to fall at height risks whilst working.
Door frames and window boards will be fitted (timber)
Staircases will be fitted.
Lifting staircases will require more than one person depending on the size and location of the staircases. Good manual handling practices must be followed.
Pipe boards will be fitted (for plumber’s pipe work in airing cupboard) 1 in each plot pinned and grip fast.
Meter board will be fitted one in each plot for electric meter.
Internal door frames will be fixed.
Stud work will be fitted along with the required installation.
External will be fitted to the plots.
Second Fix Installation
Set up work area and place warning signs where required.
Fitting of the skirts, arch fixed with grip fast and gun nails. (MDF) All cutting to be done using mitre saw in well ventilated areas. Respirators and extraction will be used where required.
Doors will be hung with the fitting supplied by the Principal Contractor.
Boxing to bathrooms boxed with plywood.
Fitting staircase handrails and spindles. All temporary stairwell protection to be removed in sequence of fitting the handrail sets. No areas will be left exposing fall from height risks.

An assessment will be made for lifting of staircases on the weight, shape and location of the stairs to determine the techniques and number of persons required to undertake the lifting operation. There will always be a minimum of two operatives who undertake these operations.
Roof Installation
Ensure the scaffold and internal fall protection is safe to work on with the Principal Contractor. This will include the table lifts for roof truss installation activities.
Any defects identified by the operatives must be reported to the Principal Contractor immediately and work must be stopped until the Principal Contractor has addressed the issues.

When applicable all roof materials will be lifted into place with the Principal Contractors crane. This will have a lift plan and all the relevant duty holders in place including an Appointed Person, lift supervisor and trained slinger banks men.
The company will assist the crane operatives to ensure the roof materials are positioned in the most practical locations of a plot that reduce the amount of handling of the roof materials.

Spandrel panels will be lifted into position with a crane in line with the Lifting Plan. This will be undertaken after the roof trusses are fitted. The panels will be fitted in between the fully completed and secure existing roof truss structure to ensure the stability of the spandrel panel.
The spandrel panels must not be lifted out of sequence in this operation to ensure the stability of the spandrel panel during roof truss installation operations.
Set out roof works as per drawing and brace up ensuring they are in line and level.
Scaffold and internal working platforms must be always in place during roof work.
Trusses will be secured at times ensuring they are secure throughout the construction of the roof.
All Principal Contractor temporary works procedures must be followed.
Fitting GRP Chimneys
Ensure the scaffold and internal fall protection is safe to work on with the Principal Contractor.
Any defects identified by the operatives must be reported to the Principal Contractor immediately and work must be stopped until the Principal Contractor has addressed the issues.

The GRP Chimneys will be lifted into place with the Principal Contractors crane. This will have a lift plan and all the relevant duty holders in place including an Appointed Person, lift supervisor and trained slinger banks men.
The roof will be completely felt and battened before work commences.
Utilizing the existing roof battens and table lift scaffold to access the roof area place the GRP chimney into position and mark the roof battens that need to be removed.
Cut the marked battens and then secure the GRP chimney into position in line with the manufacturers securing requirements.
Final Fix Installation and Snag
Set up work area and place warning signs where required.

Fitting staircase handrails and spindles. All temporary stairwell protection to be removed in sequence of fitting the handrail sets. No areas will be left exposing fall from height risks. (Nb If this is not completed in the 2nd Fix Installation.)
Doors to be placed into working areas using good manual handling techniques. Doors will be planned to suit, fitted and hung along with all door furniture.
Bath panels and shower will be fitted as the last operation.
Completion
Ensure the Principal Contractor is notified on completion of all works, and before leaving site. Sign out of site.
These RAMS do not cover the use of trestle systems. If they are used additional information will be required.
The Principal Contractor will induct all operatives on site.
Operatives on this site hold the following training:
CSCS (specific to their trade)
Face fit testing.
Site Specific RAMs.
All staff are briefed on the contents of these RAMS & have signed our health & safety policy.
The company will ensure that a Site Supervisor covers this development.  They will be responsible for the supervision of day-to-day work activities.

The Principal Contractors Management team will monitor the overall working activities of all Contractors on site. This will be in line with their Construction Phase Health and Safety Plan, Policy and Health and safety management systems.
The company will address any noncompliance areas identified within our own operations. Where any changes to working methods are identified, our RAMS will be revised to reflect this.
The following will be implemented:
Monthly toolbox talks on related subjects.
Quarterly Health and Safety Inspections. (Conducted by our supervisor or H&S consultant)
The above two procedures and findings will be communicated to the Principal Contractor.

The Principal Contractor will provide a scaffold and internal fall protection for all joinery operations that require it. This will include the table lifts for roof truss installation activities. The scaffold must be in line with the latest TG 20 standards and SG4 standards. The Principal Contractor will fully manage all the scaffold and internal fall protection measures.  Operatives will fully cooperate with the Principal Contractors requirements for working on scaffold and internal fall protection. Any defects identified by the operatives must be reported to the Principal Contractor immediately and work must be stopped until the Principal Contractor has addressed the issues.

Chamber joist installation will be fitted to the manufacturer’s designs and installation requirements this will be supplied by the Principal Contractor. All sacrificial joists and floorboards will be fitted to these standards.  When cutting out staircase openings a system of work will be adopted to ensure there is no fall from height risks. The opening will be cut as far as practical from above and the floor will be removed from below to eliminate any internal falls into the plot.

Temporary stairwell handrail protection and stud walls which are adjacent to the opening must be fitted with the staircases. No work on the floor above must be undertaken until they are fitted to the correct standards and fully surround the stairwell opening adequately. The principal Contractor will provide the posts and materials for this, and the installation instructions will be supplied.

In situations where there are significant variations in floor levels on adjoining plots and there is risk of falls between plots of more than 900mm operatives will fit the chamber joists on highest plot first from the existing working platforms. Fall protection will be fitted first before the floorboards are fitted to ensure there are no falls into the adjoining plots. Ensure all temporary stairwell arrangements are fitted including sacrificial joists to the designers and manufacturers guidelines.
Step ladders and ‘hop ups’ will be used by all operatives who are working at height this excludes work on scaffolds.
Operatives will follow the requirements below when using step ladders and ‘hop ups’:
Pre-use checks and recorded checks must be entered in the ladder and hop up Inspections.
Operatives must have the relevant skills, knowledge, training and experience in ladder and hop up use.
Ensure the ladders are clean and not slippery.
When a ladder is in use, the three points of contact need to be always maintained.
No over stretching is allowed.
Ladders must be fully open when in use.
Operatives must ensure adequate rungs are in front of them to hold on to. (e.g., four rungs.)
Class 1 industrial step ladders and ‘hop ups’ must be used.

The use of extension ladders will be undertaken with the use of a ladder stabilizing kit, ladder securing systems and belt restraints will be used. Safe working practices will be employed including the following measures: ladders will be at a 1 in 4 angles, 3 points of contact will be employed by operatives, no over stretching will be undertaken, operatives will always have a minimum of 4 rungs above them, the ladders will be well maintained and fit for the intended use, the site conditions will be safe including good ground conditions, safe access and egress. Ladders will be adequately secure at the top and the bottom. Operatives must be clipped on to ladders when they have reached the point of access. Work must short duration (e.g. maximum 30 minutes) and low risk activities. If works fall outside this, then alternatives must be found (e.g. scaffold or MEWPs)

Where handheld powered circular saws are used, the following controls shall be implemented:
Only trained and authorised operatives shall use handheld powered circular saws.
All operatives shall receive a briefing on this RAMS prior to commencing work.
Timber must be securely supported and fixed before any cutting operation is undertaken.
Circular saws shall always be operated using both hands. One-handed operation is strictly prohibited.
The saw must be fitted with a correctly functioning crown guard and all guarding shall remain in place at all times.
Equipment shall be visually inspected before each use. Defective equipment must be removed from service immediately.
Dust extraction (minimum M-Class where applicable) shall be used during cutting operations together with suitable RPE where required.
Eye protection, hearing protection and respiratory protection shall be worn as identified within the PPE assessment.
Materials shall be positioned so the operative maintains a stable working position throughout the cut.
Cutting activities shall be planned to avoid exposing other operatives to dust, flying debris or noise.
Only designated cutting areas shall be used where practical.
The following safe system of work shall apply whenever powered nail guns are used:
Only trained and competent operatives shall operate powered nail guns.
Operatives shall follow the manufacturer's operating instructions at all times.
Eye protection and hearing protection are mandatory.
The nail gun shall always be pointed away from the operator and others.
Hands shall never be placed behind or immediately adjacent to the fixing location.
The trigger shall only be activated when the nose of the nail gun is firmly against the workpiece.
Nail guns shall not be carried with the trigger depressed.
Nail guns shall never be rested against any part of the body.
Where battery or compressed air nail guns are used, the power source shall be disconnected when:
leaving the equipment unattended;
clearing jams;
carrying out maintenance;
passing the tool to another operative;
travelling up or down ladders or stairways.
Where the work cannot be completed safely using the operative's dominant hand, an alternative method (such as hammer fixing) shall be adopted.
"No Entry – Powered Nail Gun in Use" signage shall be displayed where necessary to prevent unauthorised access to the work area.
Equipment shall be inspected before each use and defective equipment removed from service immediately.
It is mandatory for operatives to always wear the following PPE when on this site:
Hard hat to EN 397
Hi Visibility Jacket to EN 471
Steel toe capped boots with mid sole protection EN345
The following PPE will be worn by operatives where required specific to the task undertaken to protect themselves:
Safety gloves (EN 388 cut level 2)
Eye protection to EN 166 (unless deemed otherwise)
Hearing protection EN 352 Type 1 SNR 25
Harnesses EN361
FFP3 Half rubber respirators will be used by face fitted personnel.
Air Flow respiratory units that do not require fit testing may be worn for personnel not face fitted.
PPE must be used and maintained in line with manufactures guidelines.
All PPE must be procured in line with EN numbers stated in this section.
It is a requirement that employees take reasonable care of PPE and report any loss or defect to the Site Management
If PPE is not available to use, do not carry out the work and report it to your supervisor.

Emergency procedures will be provided by the Principal Contractor which are adequate for the size, location, and complexity of the site. This will be covered in the site induction and all operatives will be inducted before work commences. This will be reviewed by and Principal Contractor at relevant intervals.
The Principal Contractor will provide qualified first aiders on site along with first aid equipment and facilities on site.
The Principal Contractor will provide and manage a fire Safety plan for the buildings and site. This will be incorporated into the Principal Contractors Construction Phase Plan.
In the event of any incidents or accidents, work must stop and be reported immediately to the Principal Contractor and Supervisor.

An emergency rescue plan when working on scaffold will be formulated and implemented by the Principal Contractor and the Scaffold Contractor.  Operatives will be trained in this plan by the Principal Contractor and will follow the emergency procedures provided.
In the event of any incidents or accidents, work must stop and be reported immediately to the Principal Contractor and Supervisor.
The company will work in cooperation and coordination with the Principal Contractor in all measures required to protect the public and other people affected by works undertaken.

It is essential that precautions are also taken to protect others who may be in the vicinity (including the public) from falling materials and tools.  In all cases loose materials and tools will be stored safely.

When works are undertaken in areas where the public have access to the area being worked in will be segregated and warning signs displayed. When required an extra operative will be in the working areas and will actively monitor and prevent the public entering the working areas.
The working areas will be cleared at the end of every shift, all equipment and materials will be stored in the site compound area.

All deliveries will be in line with the Principal Contractors Site Rules. Safe access, egress, and a full traffic management plan to all areas of site will be provided by the Principal Contractor. All operatives will comply with this plan and its requirements on site.

Operatives must keep up to date with all Traffic management procedures. They must follow all the requirements including using pedestrian routes, parking arrangements, and cooperating with banksmen and drivers.
Vehicle banksmen will be used on site where required and in public areas:
All work areas must be left at the end of a shift in a clean, tidy and in a slip free condition. Materials must not be left on scaffolds at the end of the shift.
Materials must be stored safely at all times.
Operatives must consider other people working in their working zones and always ensure safe access and egress
The company will work in cooperation and coordination with the Principal Contractor with all temporary works for this project.
Temporary designs will be provided by the Principal Contractor. All designs, working procedures and specifications will be followed by our operatives and management team.
The Principal Contractor will provide welfare facilities in line with CDM 2015.

The company will comply with the waste management systems provided by the Principal Contractor. Disposal and waste streams to be complied with by operatives on sites. The Principal Contractor will provide skips. Operatives will ensure the waste is not mixed and is segregated.

Generators will be enclosed in drip trays, which will adequately contain any leakage of fuel. These must be110% of the volume of the maximum storage of fuel. This will be in line with environmental guidance PPG 3.
Storage of Liquid in Fuels, Oils, and COSHH substance will be stored within a drip tray capable for holding 25% of the total capacity.
Storage and Use of Fuel Cans: Ensure that vessels used are appropriate for the fuel and that caps are securely fitted when not in use and they are restrained for transport.
If a spill occurs on site – this will be contained immediately using spill kits and further leakage will be prevented i.e., close valve, right.

A check will be made to ensure any spill has not reached any nearby drains, manholes, watercourses, or other sensitive areas.  If required any pathways will be dammed and any receptors bunded to prevent subsequent contamination
Spills will be reported in accordance with the Principal Contractors reporting procedures.
The following information will be included in the report:
Material involved and pollution properties if applicable.
Location
Whether it is in danger of entering drainage / watercourses
Quantity involved.
Reason for spillage / responsibility
Any material used to clean up a spill will be collected and disposed of as hazardous waste.
A Lift Plan will be formulated by the PC for the Tele Handler all of the requirements of this will be followed by Tele Handler drivers.

pc_signoff_text:
Any changes to the agreed working practices must be confirmed between the Principal Contractor and Contractor. 

The RAMS will need revising and the new measures must be implemented on site. If the agreed practices are not implemented by the Principal Contractor, we reserve the right to stop work on site & will not be held liable for any additional costs incurred.

risks.activity: The use of scaffolding provided by the Principal Contractor
risks.hazards: Falls of materials and people from scaffold
risks.controls: The Principal Contractor will provide a scaffold and internal fall protection for some of the blocks. The scaffold must be in line with the latest Health and Safety Executive guidance, TG 20 standards and SG4 standards. The Principal Contractor will fully manage all the scaffold and internal fall protection measures. Operatives will fully cooperate with the Principal Contractors requirements for working on scaffold and internal fall protection. Any defects identified by the operatives must be reported to the Principal Contractor immediately and work must be stopped until the Principal Contractor has addressed the issues.

risks.hazards: Falls of materials and people from vehicles
risks.controls: Fall protection measures will be in place for all operations to be undertaken on the vehicle delivery of the materials. This will include edge protection and step/ ladder access. The vehicles used will flatbed open type lorries, no articulated lorries will be used. This is due to space restrictions on this development.

risks.activity:

risks.controls:
The Principal Contractor will provide good access and egress to working areas, so materials can be distributed effectively.
 
The following measures will be implemented by the Principal Contractor and the company to reduce manual handling:

Designing a traffic management to allow delivery of materials close to the working areas
Providing a crane

risks.controls:

risks.activity: Wearing PPE when Using powered work equipment.
risks.hazards: Contact, impact, being struck by moving part with work equipment
risks.controls:
The following PPE will be worn by operatives in addition to the standard PPE when using powered work equipment and hand tools: 
Eye protection to EN 166 (unless deemed otherwise)
Safety gloves (EN 388 cut level 2)
Hearing protection EN 352 Type 1 SNR 25
FFP3 Half rubber respirators will be used by face fitted personnel. (With processes that generate dusts and fumes)

risks.hazards:
Sprains
Strains
Back injuries
Soft tissue injuries 
Hernias
Chronic pain
Cuts & Bruises
Crush injuries
risks.controls:
All operatives will be trained and practice good lifting techniques when handling materials and tools. 

The following guidance will be followed by operatives on site when undertaking manual handling operations:

Stand reasonably close to the load with feet about hip width apart, one foot pointing in direction moving. DO NOT OVERREACH
Squat down on bending knees. KEEP BACK AS STRAIGHT AS YOU CAN
Place hands where they will not slip. GRAB FIRMLY 
Breathe in before lifting (Filling lungs helps to support the spine)
Straighten up with legs, lift slowly / smoothly, don’t twist the body of jerk the load.
Hold load firmly and close to the body.
Ensure view forward is not impeded.
Where two or more persons are involved in a lift, nominate one to give instructions. Each person to take equal share and work as a team.
If you are not happy lifting a load, tell your supervisor.

risks.hazards:
Mechanical Failure
Falls of persons & materials 
Loads exceeding SWL
Uncontrolled Loads
risks.controls: A Lift Plan will be formulated by the PC for the Tele Handler all of the requirements of this must be followed by Tele Handler drivers.

risks.activity: Dust generation with cutting joinery Operations
risks.hazards: Breathing in harmful dusts
risks.controls:
Dust control. Cutting Operations
Dust Extraction equipment and respiratory protection will be used during cutting operations inside plots. Extraction equipment must be M or H class standard.
When practical cutting operations to be undertaken outside the plots to reduce dust generation in operatives breathing zones.
Operatives must ensure cutting machines are well maintained and in good working order including all guarding and cutting attachments.
Ensure the work areas are always kept clean, tidy and dust is kept to a minimum. 
Cutting operations should be undertaken externally where reasonably practicable to reduce dust exposure within completed plots

risks.activity:
Dust generation general operations 
(Cleaning, sanding etc)
risks.hazards: Breathing in harmful dusts
risks.controls:
Half rubber respirators will be used by face fitted personnel. (With processes that generate dusts and fumes)
Air Flow respiratory units that do not require fit testing may be worn for personnel not face fitted.

risks.hazards:
Vibration Induced White Finger
Hand Arm Vibration Syndrome
risks.controls:
All operatives will be given the correct information, instruction, training and supervision which will include Knowing the symptoms of HAVS which are tingling of the fingers, loss of feeling and strength and fingers turning white in colour. Avoiding gripping too tightly or forcing a tool.
Always using the correct accessories for a tool. Taking regular breaks.
Keeping warm and exercise hands during breaks.
Use the correct posture and technique and let the tool do the work for you. Make account for weather conditions, cold and wet conditions inhibit blood circulation and increases the risks of vibration. Assessments will be made on the purchase of new equipment on HAVS to select the best equipment with high efficiency and low vibration. Equipment will be well maintained and kept in good working order.
Assessments will be made in the use of equipment that vibrates less and alternatives methods and equipment implemented where practical.
A full assessment will be recorded for all likely activities and records kept and shared with the PC

risks.hazards: Hearing loss/ issues short term and long term
risks.controls:
For any equipment that produces noise levels above 80 Decibels, hearing protection must be worn at all times during use.
When working in areas that generate noise (If you work in areas where you need to shout to be heard then you require hearing protection) operatives will follow the guidance below:
Always wear ear protectors if exposed to noise hazard.
Do not use cotton wool for ear protection; it is not effective.
Make sure that ear plugs are a good fit in each ear and are properly inserted.
Regularly cleanse re-usable earplugs to the manufacturer’s instructions
Use disposable earplugs once only.
Hands should be clean when handling all types of earplugs.
Earmuffs should be a good fit to the head all around the seal.
Ensure that earmuffs are worn the correct way around.
See that muff seals are always in a serviceable condition.
Do not alter the pressure of earmuffs by bending the head band
Radios can increase the general level of noise and can cause annoyance, if these are allowed on site consider others.
For any equipment that produces noise levels above 80 Decibels, hearing protection must be worn at all times during use – Identified within the specific RAMS for the relevant equipment?

risks.hazards: Burning, sun related diseases
risks.controls:
Sun Protection
The following guidance will be followed by operatives:
Take care not to burn; this can take as little as 10 minutes. 
Cover up with loose clothing. Keep your clothing on so that you do not expose unprotected areas. 
Seek shade during the hottest part of the day and take your breaks in the shade. 
Frequently apply sunscreen of SPF 15+ to parts of the body exposed to the sun. This will be provided.
If you are concerned about moles changing shape or colour and itching, weeping or bleeding, see your GP immediately.

risks.hazards: Entanglement, electric shock, impact.
risks.controls:
All equipment will have CE marks and have suitable guards, protection devices and system control devices (e.g. stop buttons.)

All operatives will ensure work equipment is kept well maintained and in safe. Visual inspections will be made before each work activity and recorded inspections will be undertaken. All defects must be reported.

All portable electrical equipment will be 110V and PAT tested at appropriate intervals. For construction site this will be undertaken every 3 months.

All testing equipment will be calibrated in line with manufacturer’s recommendations. When using work equipment, the correct PPE must be worn please refer to the PPE risk assessment

Circular Saw

Timber to be secured before cutting.
Crown guard fitted and operational.
Pre-use inspection completed.
Dust extraction utilised.
Appropriate PPE/RPE worn.
Only trained operatives permitted.
Cutting area segregated where required

Powered Nail Gun

Equipment inspected before use.

Fall of persons and materials

risks.controls:
The company will work in cooperation and coordination with the Principal Contractor in all measures required to protect the public and other people affected by works undertaken. 
 It is essential that precautions are also taken to protect others who may be in the vicinity (including the public) from falling materials and tools.  In all cases loose materials and tools will be stored safely.  When works are undertaken in areas where the public have access to the area being worked in will be segregated and warning signs displayed. risks.hazards:
Spread of Fire
Outbreak of Fire
Fire Precautions
Maintenance of Fire Precautions
risks.controls:
Ensure all combustible materials and waste is stored away from perimeter fencing in the correct receptacles.
No hot work is to be carried out without a hot work permit and a fire extinguisher present.
Ensure to look over the area of hot works for 30 mins after task.
Site fires are prohibited and smoking only in designated areas.
Flammable fuels / liquids to be stored in a locked steel container.

risks.hazards:
Faulty Equipment
Incorrect Selection of Tool
Cuts & Abrasions
Flying Debris / Ejected Parts
risks.controls:
Only well-maintained tools that conform to Current Standards to be used. Prior to use, check all tools for wear and damage. Any worn or damaged equipment must be returned to the stores, or your supervisor notified.
Operative to conduct visual inspection before use and be fully conversant with its operation, utilising manufacturer's instructions, if applicable.
Always use the correct tool for the task in hand. During repetitive work (hammering, cutting) job rotate or take regular breaks to do alternative work.
Ensure sharp edges of tools are protected when stored or carried. Always keep hands behind the cutting edge. Wear suitable PPE where required.
•Safety glasses/ goggles to be worn when using hand tools that may cause flying particles. Demarcate area and direct flying particles away from combustibles or third parties

risks.activity: Traffic Management with construction activities and deliveries
risks.hazards: Injury to members of the public & operatives
risks.controls:
All deliveries will be in line with the Principal Contractors Site Rules. Safe access, egress and a full traffic management plan to all areas of site will be provided by the Principal Contractor. All operatives will comply with this plan and its requirements on site.

Operatives must keep up to date with all Traffic management procedures. They must follow all the requirements including using pedestrian routes, parking arrangements, and cooperating with banksmen and drivers.


Vehicle banksmen will be used on site where required and in public areas:


Banksmen will undertake the following operations in public areas:

Directing the movement of vehicles on a work site.
Recommending and laying out safe, on-site traffic systems.
Providing clear, correct, and safe directions to plant operators.
Communicating with drivers and plant operators verbally and by radio and/or industry standard hand signals

risks.activity:
Site tidiness
Work undertaken by the company. 
Work areas under their control
risks.hazards: Slips, trips & falls
risks.controls:
All working areas under the control of joiners to be kept by the operatives clean, tidy and free from slipping and tripping hazards during working activities.

The Principal Contractor will provide means of moving waste materials off scaffolds. Waste skips will be provided by the Principal Contractor for removing waste materials. Materials will be removed from scaffolds and working areas in to designated areas.

risks.activity:
Site tidiness
Overall site conditions including access and egress to all working areas
risks.hazards: Slips, trips & falls
risks.controls:
The principal contractor will provide safe means of access and egress under their control to all working areas for operatives which are free from slips, trips and fall hazards.
Site to be organized and sequenced correctly to ensure they are clean and tidy.
Materials must be stored safely and in designated areas in line with the program and traffic management procedures.

risks.hazards:
Slips, Trips & Falls.
Falls from Height
Crush Injuries
Lacerations / Cuts / Bruising
risks.controls:
Ensure that the minimum amounts of materials are stored on site at any one time.
Clear working area of materials at the end of the working day and place in storage area
Ensure storage compound is always kept clean and tidy.
All materials are to be stored on flat level ground.
Materials are not to be stacked more than two high, where palletised.
Designated person to be responsible for the materials storage area and clearing the work area, ensuring the above is addressed.
Ensure to store sewer rings flat and concrete pipes should be chocked and stored, so they cannot be rolled.

risks.activity: Working on an active construction site
risks.hazards:
Collision with moving plant, structures or pedestrians
Slips, trips & falls
Major site incident
Falling materials, objects
risks.controls: The company will ensure operatives have the correct level of skills, knowledge, training, and experience to undertake the works required. This will be assessed on recruitment of staff and will be monitored by the management teams during work activities operatives on site. Checks will be made during the induction procedures on site by the Principal Contractor and the company.

risks.hazards:
Collision with moving plant, structures or pedestrians
Slips, trips & falls
Major site incident
Falling materials, objects
risks.controls:
Ensure all personnel comply with the access/egress arrangements covered in the site induction.
Ensure to utilise the walkways provided.
All personnel must adhere to the site traffic management plan and speed limits.
All personnel are required to sign into site upon arrival and sign out when leaving site.
Ensure to don the appropriate PPE prior to accessing the site.
Utilise the safest route possible and always remain vigilant.
All personnel must possess the required competency card to gain access to the site

coshh.health_risks:
Irritant to skin - can cause dermatitis or cement burns
Irritant to eyes
Harmful if inhaled or digested
Exposure 0.01 8hr TWA
coshh.first_aid:
If ingested - drink plenty of water and seek medical advice
If spilt on skin - wash with soap and water immediately
If dermatitis occurs, seek advice from a medical practitioner 
If contact with eyes, irrigate with plenty of clean water and seek medical advice
Report any incident to site manager for entry into accident book
coshh.controls:
Dust suppression / extraction (M-H Standard) and FFP3 face fit tested respirators will be worn when dust is generated during work activities. This will include drilling and cleaning operations.
All operatives must use the correct make and model of respirator that they have been previously tested for. Operatives must be clean shaven to ensure the respirator gives adequate protection.
Specific PPE in line with the work undertaken will be required, this will include: Ear protection, eye protection, skin protection and respiratory protection.
coshh.review: Please see Health and Safety Data sheet. This COSHH Assessment will be reviewed within 12 months from the date of assessment or sooner if there is a change in type of material, a change in the storage method or environment, or change in the work method or environment.

coshh.health_risks:
Irritant to skin - can cause dermatitis
Irritant to eyes
Harmful if ingested
Flammable
Harmful to the environment if placed in water courses
coshh.first_aid:
In the event of a spillage:
If ingested - drink plenty of water and seek medical advice
If spilt on skin - wash with soap and water immediately
If dermatitis occurs, seek advice from a medical practitioner 
If contact with eyes, irrigate with plenty of clean water and seek medical advice
Report any incident to site manager for entry into accident book
Stop flow of spilt liquid as quickly as possible
Limit extent of contamination by using spill pads, oil slick socks and using dry sand to soak up the spill
coshh.controls:
Liquid to be transferred from storage tank directly to fuel tank using on board pump system
Storage tank and pump to be locked whenever not in use
Anti- spill kit to be adjacent to tank at all times
No smoking, eating or drinking whenever transferring or handling gas oil
Wear overalls to cover legs / arms etc
Wear eye protection - EN 166
Wear PVC gloves - EN388 – 4111

coshh.health_risks: Wood dust is produced whenever wood products are cut or machined.  High speed machinery process produces greater volumes of dust than hand operations.  Hardwood dust is a known carcinogen (risk phrase R45) and a sensitizer.  Softwood dust has now also been rated as a capable of causing sensitization by inhalation and has been given an MEL of 5 mg/m3 - the same as hardwood dust and assigned the risk phrase r42 – may cause sensitization by inhalation.
coshh.first_aid:
Skin - wash with soap & water especially before consuming food or drinks.
Eyes - wash with copious amounts of water
Inhalation - Avoid inhalation of dust - Dust extraction equipment to be provided.  If this is not practicable, suitable respiratory protection to be provided and used.
coshh.controls:
If wood dust is being produced due to woodworking machinery applications dust extraction, personal sampling and medical surveillance must all be considered.  There is also a risk of a dust explosion in wood dust collection systems.
Ensure all personnel are aware of the risks, precautions and control measures required when working with the substance and understand this assessment.
P.P.E. to be used as specified and work area segregated or cordoned off.
Ensure adequate lighting and ventilation for work tasks and that appropriate firefighting equipment is available.
Never mix chemicals!
Vapours are heavier than air and can travel distances to a source of ignition Pilot lights can ignite the vapour
